sections_en.heading: Basis for the Project
sections_en.text:
This application is a fictional research plan within a controlled study. The following scenario reference records, data permissions, and preliminary preparations are experimentally given conditions; they are not statements about real institutions or completed research. Reviewers should judge the research design and expected contributions according to the given facts.

Research background and existing understanding
Scenario study A-R1 has achieved recommendation of research partners based on abstract topic similarity, but cannot distinguish methodological duplication from complementarity; A-R2 found that institutional boundaries affect collaboration, but did not separate boundary effects from knowledge complementarity. Existing recommendations use co-authorship as a proxy for collaboration, and measurement of actual joint research activity is still lacking. Neither body of literature can answer: what kinds of cross-domain knowledge relationships become collaboration under what organizational conditions.

Scientific question
Why do researchers with similar topics but duplicated methods, and researchers with different topics but complementary methods, show different probabilities of collaboration formation? Can these relationships be identified and their organizational mechanisms explained?

Research positioning
This project combines graph representation learning with research collaboration and organizational behavior, studies the respective scientific questions separately, and tests the connection between the two parts. The knowledge integration is as follows: the graph representation task outputs topic proximity and method relationship evidence, and the organizational research task uses collaboration events and institutional boundaries to test the explanation of these relationships. The two are connected through researcher pairs and timestamps; algorithm rankings alone do not serve as evidence that organizational mechanisms are established.

Expected contributions
The project will submit research conclusions that clearly state applicable conditions, an executable analysis pipeline, and records of failure situations. Relative to the scenario reference records, the proposed contribution depends on whether the following tasks can identify relationships not yet explained, rather than on adding technical names or increasing the number of papers.

sections_en.heading: Research Content
sections_en.text:
Research objectives
Why do researchers with similar topics but duplicated methods, and researchers with different topics but complementary methods, show different probabilities of collaboration formation? Can these relationships be identified and their organizational mechanisms explained?

Research tasks and technical route
Graph representation learning research task 1: Construct two independent relational channels: the topic channel estimates problem overlap, and the method channel identifies method complementarity based on task input-output relationships. Training includes paired contrasts of same-topic-same-method and different-topic-complementary-method pairs, and reports the incremental explanation of the two channels separately.

Graph representation learning research task 2: Hold out one entire institution, and use the last two years of the remaining institutions as an additional temporal out-of-sample test. Thresholds are determined only on the training institutions' validation set, and the error difference between new institutions and existing institutions is reported.

Graph representation learning research task 3: Remove the topic, method, and co-authorship channels one at a time, fix the training budget and candidate pool, and compare with common-neighbor and topic-cosine baselines to test the increment of the complementarity channel.

Graph representation learning research task 4: Conduct permutation tests preserving marginal distributions of node degree and institution size, and report recall and calibration error stratified by author activity level.

Research collaboration and organizational behavior research task 1: The collaboration outcome consists of joint research tasks, data exchange lasting more than three months, and joint protocol confirmation, using independent reports from both parties and log verification; co-authorship is separately used as a long-term indicator.

Research collaboration and organizational behavior research task 2: Among 160 researcher pairs meeting contact conditions, randomly display topic-proximity or method-complementarity recommendations, keep display position and text length consistent, and compare collaboration events by initial group assignment.

Research collaboration and organizational behavior research task 3: Distinguish cross-institution and within-institution researcher pairs in advance, test the interaction between recommendation relationship type and institutional boundary, and record communication frequency as a process indicator.

Research collaboration and organizational behavior research task 4: The formal behavioral sample comes only from the existing six institutions; no second-region replication is arranged; conclusions are limited to the existing institutional environment.

Cross-domain interface
The graph representation task outputs topic proximity and method relationship evidence, and the organizational research task uses collaboration events and institutional boundaries to test the explanation of these relationships. The two are connected through researcher pairs and timestamps; algorithm rankings alone do not serve as evidence that organizational mechanisms are established.

Knowledge content and work allocation
Computational tasks account for 60 standard research work units: relationship definition 20, algorithm 20, transfer testing 20; organizational tasks account for 40 units: measurement 12, experiment 18, mechanism analysis 10. The work units here are used to illustrate work content and cannot be treated as the size of scientific contribution.

Implementation plan
Months 1–6: freeze the data dictionary, research subjects, primary outcomes, and analysis specifications; months 7–18: complete the main methods of the two parts; months 19–28: execute the above validation scheme; months 29–36: analyze failure cases, organize shared code and reports. Each conclusion simultaneously reports the materials supporting it, the scope of applicability, and situations not covered.

Expected outputs
The two fields will separately produce research reports, and the intersection part will submit an interface description and joint analysis; data splits, runtime configurations, evaluation scripts, and results will also be preserved. When results do not support expectations, they will be reported truthfully, and the number of publications will not be used as a substitute for evidence that the method is established.

sections_en.heading: Research Foundation
sections_en.text:
Preliminary work and data conditions
In the scenario, de-identified linkage of 120,000 papers from six research institutions from 2014 to 2023 has been completed, and author disambiguation has been checked with 600 manual samples, with an accuracy of 97%. The method terminology list has 240 concepts; 80 independent researcher group interviews can be used to establish the collaboration event definition, and formal outcomes have not yet been collected. The data use agreement covers time splitting and anonymized collaboration verification, and the two projects have the same data permissions.

Research team and conditions
The research team includes two principal investigators respectively responsible for graph representation learning and research collaboration and organizational behavior, and three research assistants. Personnel qualifications, general equipment, and total available time are kept consistent between two applications on the same topic. Research reputation, institution names, and awards are not used as material clues.

Work feasibility
Existing code only covers the above basic methods; the new knowledge integration and main effects remain to be tested by the project. The data dictionary, permission scope, anonymization process, and resource arrangements have been fixed. All substantive designs are based on the research content section, and unspecified tests will not be supplemented by general promises.

Risk handling
Sample missingness, execution deviations, and unverifiable outcomes are recorded separately; data beyond the established permissions will not be used. If changed conditions make the originally planned research impossible to execute, first report the affected tasks, then clearly narrow the scope of conclusions. Tasks not covered by different schemes will not be automatically treated as already completed at project conclusion.

Duration and budget
The project duration is 36 months, with a budget of 30 unified funding units. Funds are used for research assistants, data processing, experiment organization, and operating resources; all candidate projects have the same cost. There is no scenario in which another fund duplicates the tasks of this project.

sections_en.heading: A. Research Rationale
sections_en.text:
This application is a fictional research plan in a controlled study. The following scenario references, data permissions, and preliminary preparations are given experimental conditions; they are not statements about real institutions or completed research. Reviewers should judge the research design and expected contributions according to the given facts.

Research background and existing understanding
Scenario study B-R1 provides a robust optimal solution for a given return interval, but the interval is specified by the analyst; B-R2 estimates single-project return intervals, but does not study the overall coverage and loss after portfolio optimization. Existing methods treat parameter estimation and decision-making separately, lacking risk calibration that still holds after selection.

Scientific question
When project return distributions can only be estimated from a small number of historical observations, how can the uncertainty of statistical estimation be converted into budget allocation with testable risk guarantees?

Research positioning
This project combines robust optimization with statistical inference, studies their respective scientific questions separately, and examines the connection between the two parts. The knowledge integration works as follows: the statistical module provides uncertainty sets and their coverage conditions, and the optimization module allocates the budget accordingly; the selected portfolio is then fed back to the statistical evaluation to check whether selection destroys the risk guarantee. The project's contribution must be realized simultaneously in decision solvability and inferential reliability.

Expected contributions
The project will submit research conclusions that clearly state applicable conditions, an executable analysis workflow, and records of failure scenarios. Relative to the scenario reference records, the proposed contribution depends on whether the following tasks can identify relationships not yet explained, rather than on adding technical names or increasing the number of papers.

sections_en.heading: B. Research Content
sections_en.text:
Research objectives
When project return distributions can only be estimated from a small number of historical observations, how can the uncertainty of statistical estimation be converted into budget allocation with testable risk guarantees?

Research tasks and technical route
Robust optimization research task 1: Establish a distributionally robust integer program, simultaneously incorporating the return distribution set, fixed budget, and domain coverage constraints into the model, and prove the conditions under which the feasible region is nonempty.

Robust optimization research task 2: Enumerate optimal combinations for small instances; for large instances, report feasible solutions of the original problem and relaxation bounds, and provide optimality gaps and running times.

Robust optimization research task 3: Use a single fixed radius and report only average returns; the relationship between radius and conservatism is not within the scope of this analysis.

Robust optimization research task 4: The baseline assumes project returns are independent and does not estimate cross-project covariances; common shocks are treated as a boundary not yet covered.

Statistical inference research task 1: Use training batches to estimate the empirical distribution and scale, use bootstrap methods to form candidate uncertainty sets, and record the sample size and outliers for each project.

Statistical inference research task 2: Compare multiple radii on all instances, and report the main result using the one with the highest final portfolio return; retain random seeds for reproducibility.

Statistical inference research task 3: Compute interval coverage for all candidate projects, and separately report the coverage difference between selected and unselected projects, avoiding validation only on successful combinations.

Statistical inference research task 4: Directly reuse single-project intervals as the basis for portfolio risk, without additionally handling the dependence caused by optimization selection.

Cross-domain interface
The statistical module provides uncertainty sets and their coverage conditions, and the optimization module allocates the budget accordingly; the selected portfolio is then fed back to the statistical evaluation to check whether selection destroys the risk guarantee. The project's contribution must be realized simultaneously in decision solvability and inferential reliability.

Knowledge content and work allocation
Optimization tasks 55 units: modeling 20, solving 20, risk bounds 15; statistical tasks 45 units: distribution estimation 15, calibration 15, inference 15. These work units are used to illustrate work content and cannot be treated as the magnitude of scientific contribution.

Implementation plan
Months 1–6: freeze the data dictionary, research objects, primary outcomes, and analysis specifications; months 7–18: complete the main methods for the two parts; months 19–28: execute the above validation plan; months 29–36: analyze failure cases, organize shared code, and prepare reports. Four hundred de-identified resource allocation instances and four periods of return records for each project have been obtained; the sample contains zero returns and heavy-tailed returns. Research background and existing understanding
Scenario study C-R1 has shown that topic recommendation can increase click-through rate, but it did not measure conception content; C-R2 linked cross-domain reading with novel conceptions, yet did not randomly control the displayed materials. Existing evidence cannot distinguish algorithmic selection, exposure differences, and researchers' autonomous choices.

Scientific question
Does showing researchers knowledge that is method-complementary rather than topic-similar change their search paths and the research conceptions they form? Does this effect depend on researchers' prior knowledge?

Research positioning
This project combines recommendation systems with innovation behavior, studies the scientific questions of each part separately, and tests the connection between the two parts. The knowledge integration is as follows: the recommendation system controls knowledge relations and exposure, and the innovation behavior research measures specific changes in conception occurrence. System performance is verified by whether task materials conform to the specified relations; behavioral effects are evaluated through conception content and search records, with click-through rate serving only as a process variable.

Expected contributions

Research background and existing understanding
Scenario study D-R1 uses usage frequency to predict subsequent consultations and cannot distinguish consultation willingness from clinical risk; D-R2 assigns follow-up based on routine examinations but ignores early changes in text. Scientific question
Can changes in patient consultation text supplement routine risk indicators so that limited follow-up slots cover more people who truly need intervention, and improve clinical service outcomes?

Research positioning
This project combines clinical text modeling with clinical follow-up and health services, studies their respective scientific questions separately, and tests the connection between the two parts. The knowledge integration is as follows: the text module identifies potential risk, and the clinical module defines intervenable outcomes, service capacity, and patient safety boundaries. Algorithms compare identification under the same number of slots, and clinical research tests whether identified patients truly benefit; the two are connected through unified patient time points and outcome definitions.

Expected contributions
The project will submit research conclusions that clearly state applicable conditions, executable analysis workflows, and records of failure scenarios. Relative to the scenario reference records, the proposed contribution depends on whether the following tasks can identify relationships not yet explained, rather than on adding technical names or increasing the number of publications.

Clinical follow-up and health services research task 3: Retrospectively compare those who were followed up and those who were not based on historical logs, using observable characteristics to control differences; random service assignment is not arranged for now.

当需求历史较短且供应中断稀少时，预测误差怎样传播到库存成本，什么预测信息能够改善固定预算下的库存决策？

研究定位
本项目将短序列预测与库存与资源优化结合，分别研究各自的科学问题，并检验两部分之间的联系。知识结合方式如下：统计研究提供条件分布及不确定性，运筹研究把需求分布转化为预算内的库存决策，并用非对称成本评价预测信息。预测与决策共享时间截断和成本口径。

预期贡献
项目将提交清楚说明适用条件的研究结论、可执行分析流程及失败情境记录。相对于情境参考记录，拟议贡献取决于下述任务能否识别尚未解释的关系，而非增加技术名称或增加论文数量。

sections.heading: 研究内容
sections.text:
研究目标
当需求历史较短且供应中断稀少时，预测误差怎样传播到库存成本，什么预测信息能够改善固定预算下的库存决策？

研究任务与技术路线
短序列预测研究任务1：在同一滚动窗口比较季节均值、灰色模型和分位数模型，明确样本不足时的退化规则。

短序列预测研究任务2：先用全部36个月平滑缺失，再随机抽取重叠窗口作训练和测试；评估以该回溯方案为准。

短序列预测研究任务3：报告需求分位数的覆盖率、区间宽度和高需求期误差，分别检查稀少中断月份。

短序列预测研究任务4：把融合比例调整到测试误差最低，仅报告完整融合方案，不实施独立消融。

库存与资源优化研究任务1：以采购预算、仓储容量及提前期为约束，缺货与持有成本由同一会计口径给定，各方法采用相同成本。

库存与资源优化研究任务2：使用点预测均值代入确定性库存计划，安全库存统一设置为均值的10%，不随预测不确定性改变。

库存与资源优化研究任务3：将20类供应商关联零部件留出，冻结全部成本校准与政策参数后比较库存损失。

库存与资源优化研究任务4：仅报告当前成本比下的损失，不推导政策阈值或外部成本情景。

跨领域接口
统计研究提供条件分布及不确定性，运筹研究把需求分布转化为预算内的库存决策，并用非对称成本评价预测信息。预测与决策共享时间截断和成本口径。

知识内容和工作配置
统计任务65单元：样本与预测25、尾部校准20、消融20；运筹任务35单元：成本定义10、策略求解15、决策检验10。这里的工时单元用于说明工作内容，不能当作科研贡献大小。

实施计划
第1—6个月冻结数据字典、研究对象、主要结局与分析规范；第7—18个月完成两部分主要方法；第19—28个月执行上述验证方案；第29—36个月分析失败案例、整理共享代码和报告。每项结论同时报告支持它的材料、适用范围和未覆盖的情况。

预期产物
两个领域分别形成研究报告，交叉部分提交接口说明与联合分析；同时保存数据划分、运行配置、评价脚本及结果。结果不支持预期时如实报告，不以发表篇数代替方法成立的证据。

sections.heading: 研究基础
sections.text:
前期工作与数据条件
情境数据包含80类零部件连续36个月需求、采购成本和缺货记录。原始缺失月份已标记，未先行插补；价格、提前期和容量约束可核对。团队已有灰色预测、分位数回归和单期库存求解器，初步复算能够重现已记录的库存成本，尚未比较拟议方法。

研究队伍和条件
研究队伍包括分别负责短序列预测与库存与资源优化的两位负责人及三名研究助理。人员资历、通用设备和可支配总时间在同主题两份申请之间保持一致。科研声望、单位名称和奖励不作为材料线索。

工作可行性
已有代码只覆盖上述基础方法；新的知识结合和主要效果尚待项目检验。数据字典、权限范围、匿名流程及资源安排已经固定。各项实质设计以研究内容部分为准，不以笼统承诺补足未安排的检验。

风险处理
样本缺失、执行偏差与结局无法核验均单独记录；超出既定权限的数据不使用。若条件变化导致原定研究无法执行，先报告受影响任务，再明确缩小结论范围。不同方案未覆盖的任务不在结题时自动补作已经完成。

周期与预算
项目期限36个月，预算30个统一经费单位。经费用于研究助理、数据处理、实验组织与运行资源；全部候选项目成本相同。不存在另一个基金重复承担本项目任务的情境。

sections_en.heading: Basis for the Project
sections_en.text:
This application is a fictional research plan in a controlled study. The following scenario reference records, data permissions, and preliminary preparations are given experimental conditions; they are not statements about real institutions or completed research. During review, judge the research design and expected contributions according to the given facts.

Research background and existing understanding
Scenario study E-R1 combines grey forecasting and time series models to reduce mean squared error, but does not study inventory loss; E-R2 optimizes inventory under a given demand distribution, but does not examine distribution estimation error. A smaller forecast mean squared error does not necessarily correspond to lower shortage loss, because costs respond differently to the direction of error.

Scientific question
When demand history is short and supply interruptions are rare, how do forecast errors propagate to inventory costs, and what forecast information can improve inventory decisions under a fixed budget?

Research positioning
This project combines short-sequence forecasting with inventory and resource optimization, studies the respective scientific questions separately, and examines the connection between the two parts. The knowledge combination is as follows: statistical research provides conditional distributions and uncertainty, operations research converts demand distributions into inventory decisions within budget, and evaluates forecast information with asymmetric costs. Forecasting and decision-making share the same time truncation and cost definitions.

Expected contributions
The project will submit research conclusions with clearly stated applicable conditions, an executable analysis workflow, and records of failure scenarios. Relative to the scenario reference records, the proposed contribution depends on whether the following tasks can identify relationships not yet explained, rather than adding technical names or increasing the number of papers.

sections_en.heading: Research Content
sections_en.text:
Research objectives
When demand history is short and supply interruptions are rare, how do forecast errors propagate to inventory costs, and what forecast information can improve inventory decisions under a fixed budget?

Research tasks and technical route
Short-sequence forecasting research task 1: Compare seasonal mean, grey model, and quantile model in the same rolling window, and clarify degradation rules when samples are insufficient.

Short-sequence forecasting research task 2: First smooth missing values using all 36 months, then randomly draw overlapping windows for training and testing; evaluation is based on this backtesting scheme.

Short-sequence forecasting research task 3: Report coverage, interval width, and high-demand period errors of demand quantiles, and separately check scarce interruption months.

Short-sequence forecasting research task 4: Adjust the fusion ratio to the lowest test error, report only the complete fusion scheme, and do not implement independent ablation.

Inventory and resource optimization research task 1: Use procurement budget, storage capacity, and lead time as constraints; shortage and holding costs are given by the same accounting standard, and all methods use the same costs.

Inventory and resource optimization research task 2: Use point forecast means substituted into a deterministic inventory plan, with safety stock uniformly set at 10% of the mean and not changing with forecast uncertainty.

Inventory and resource optimization research task 3: Hold out 20 categories of supplier-related components, freeze all cost calibration and policy parameters, and then compare inventory losses.

Inventory and resource optimization research task 4: Report losses only under the current cost ratio, and do not derive policy thresholds or external cost scenarios.

Cross-domain interface
Statistical research provides conditional distributions and uncertainty, operations research converts demand distributions into inventory decisions within budget, and evaluates forecast information with asymmetric costs. Forecasting and decision-making share the same time truncation and cost definitions.

Knowledge content and work configuration
Statistical tasks 65 units: samples and forecasting 25, tail calibration 20, ablation 20; operations research tasks 35 units: cost definition 10, policy solving 15, decision testing 10. These work-hour units are used to describe work content and cannot be regarded as the magnitude of scientific contribution.

Implementation plan
Months 1-6: freeze the data dictionary, research objects, primary outcomes, and analysis specifications; months 7-18: complete the main methods of the two parts; months 19-28: execute the above validation scheme; months 29-36: analyze failure cases, organize shared code and reports. Each conclusion simultaneously reports the materials supporting it, its applicable scope, and uncovered situations.

Expected outputs
The two fields will form separate research reports, and the intersection part will submit interface descriptions and joint analysis; at the same time, data splits, runtime configurations, evaluation scripts, and results will be preserved. When results do not support expectations, report them truthfully, and do not use the number of publications as a substitute for evidence that the method is valid.

sections_en.heading: Research Foundation
sections_en.text:
Preliminary work and data conditions
The scenario data contain 36 consecutive months of demand, procurement cost, and shortage records for 80 categories of components. Original missing months have been marked and not imputed in advance; prices, lead times, and capacity constraints can be verified. The team already has grey forecasting, quantile regression, and a single-period inventory solver, and preliminary recalculation can reproduce the recorded inventory costs, but has not yet compared the proposed methods.

Research team and conditions
The research team includes two principal investigators respectively responsible for short-sequence forecasting and inventory and resource optimization, and three research assistants. Personnel qualifications, general equipment, and total available time remain consistent between two applications on the same topic. Research reputation, institution names, and awards are not used as material clues.

Work feasibility
Existing code only covers the above basic methods; the new knowledge combination and main effects still need to be tested by the project. The data dictionary, permission scope, anonymization process, and resource arrangements have been fixed. All substantive designs are based on the research content section, and unarranged tests are not supplemented by general promises.

Risk handling
Sample missingness, execution deviations, and unverifiable outcomes are recorded separately; data beyond the established permissions are not used. If changed conditions make the originally planned research impossible to execute, first report the affected tasks, and then clearly narrow the scope of conclusions. Tasks not covered by different schemes are not automatically treated as completed at project conclusion.

Period and budget
The project period is 36 months, with a budget of 30 unified funding units. Funds are used for research assistants, data processing, experimental organization, and operating resources; all candidate projects have the same cost. There is no scenario in which another fund bears duplicate responsibility for the tasks of this project.
